marks.assessment:
## The name

VENQORI is the consumer-facing house and product name for the client's water-quality monitoring app and the online training bundled with it — the name on the app-store listing and on the whole offering, not a feature or a tier inside a larger line. As a string it is invented: Latinate in shape, dictionary-empty, and carrying no water, testing or environmental meaning that a competitor could already be using. That matters more than it may appear. A fanciful name has no descriptive core for anyone else to be sitting on, so the risk it carries is not the usual risk of shared vocabulary — it is the narrower risk of a coined neighbour that looks or sounds close.

## What the landscape looks like

- Nothing using the exact name was identified in the app-store, marketplace and general web results screened: no app, no company, no training or water-testing service, no software offering.
- The water-quality apps that did surface are named descriptively or by acronym. VENQORI does not participate in that naming convention, which means it is not competing for distinctiveness inside a crowd of similar titles.
- No famous mark, cultural property or entertainment reference using the exact term was identified, and no negative or reputationally charged association attaches to it.
- The closest located strings are coined corporate names — one an industrial manufacturer across textiles, packaging, machinery and automation, the other a pharmaceutical and consumer-healthcare business. Both are carried below as findings at the lowest band rather than set aside, because a one-letter or one-consonant difference is close enough that the reviewing lawyer should see it named.

## What drives the rating

The rating turns on the two halves of the comparison moving in the same direction. On the name side, the neighbours are genuinely close as strings but neither is the mark: one adds a trailing vowel, the other swaps the consonant. On the goods side, industrial manufacturing and pharmaceuticals are remote from a consumer app that records water readings and from bundled online training — different shelves, different buyers, different channels. Where a coined mark meets no on-field user of the name and only off-field users of near-neighbours, the screen does not produce a blocker.

What holds the read where it is rather than lower is that closeness itself: a single trailing letter separates the mark from an operating multinational, and the .com at the exact name did not resolve on retrieval, so nothing rules out an inactive holder behind it.

## What to do with it

Treat VENQORI as not knocked out at this depth and let it proceed to clearance. Two things are worth carrying forward into that next stage: whether either near-neighbour has any software, environmental-testing or training activity beyond the trade described in the screened material, and the ownership and status of the exact-name domain, which this screen established only as non-resolving.
